input: Audience: Wedding photographers serving more than one region who are deciding how to focus advertising and landing-page content while managing a limited initial scope. | Tension: A shared page may be convenient, but imagery and context that suit one region may not speak to couples considering a different setting. | Argument: When a wedding business serves regions with different visual expectations, a market-specific landing page can make the offer easier to evaluate than asking one page to represent both markets at once. | Take: Treat geographic expansion and page design as linked choices: a business can start with the market it is prioritising and revisit the second market when it can represent that audience coherently. | Mechanism: In the reported discussion, the photographer said Colorado couples often want to see mountains while Florida couples often do not, and connected that difference to difficulty targeting both through one landing page. Different visual expectations can change what makes the page feel relevant to a couple evaluating the location. | Reader decision: Check whether each target region has meaningfully different visual expectations or reasons to choose the business, then decide whether one page can represent them or whether to focus first on one market.
